stimulus.text: Paraphrase of President Washington’s Neutrality Proclamation, April 22, 1793: with France and Great Britain at war, the United States would be friendly and impartial toward both sides and would not take part in the fighting. Many Americans wanted to help France, pointing to the 1778 treaty of alliance and to French help in the American Revolution.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrased from George Washington, Neutrality Proclamation, April 22, 1793. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from George Washington, Neutrality Proclamation, April 22, 1793, public domain.
stem: When Citizen Genêt, the French minister, fitted out privateers in American ports in 1793, Washington’s response most directly showed that the government would do what?

options.text: Arrest every French citizen living in the United States.
options.misconception: Background: Washington did not order the arrest of French citizens in general.

options.text: Enforce neutrality even against France, the nation’s old ally.
Ask Congress to declare war on Great Britain at once.
options.misconception: Washington sought to stay out of the war, not to declare one.

options.text: Give France the use of American ports for the whole war.
options.misconception: Letting France use the ports would have broken neutrality, not enforced it.

rationales.B: Background: Genêt acted as if the old alliance let France use American ports, and Washington demanded his recall and stopped the privateers.
rationales.A: The response targeted the privateers, not French citizens in general.
rationales.C: Washington sought to stay out of the war, not to declare one.
rationales.D: Letting France use the ports would have broken neutrality, not enforced it.
rationales.general:
1. The proclamation made the United States impartial toward both France and Britain.
2. Background: Genêt, the French minister, acted as if the old alliance let France fit out privateers in American ports, and Washington demanded his recall and stopped the ships.
3. Stopping France’s ships proved neutrality applied to the old ally as well as to the old enemy.
4. So the response showed the government would enforce its own policy, even against France.
Remember: neutrality is proved by saying no to your friends, not only to your enemies.
